    Jeffrey Leiser v. John Bretzel, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-25-02424 / USCOURTS-ca7-25-02424-0

    FAPD-AI: In a nonprecedential order, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for prison officials in Jeffrey Leiser's suit under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, which alleged that his disciplinary segregation violated due process under the Fourteenth Amendment. Assuming a liberty interest, the court found that Leiser received adequate notice of the conduct report, that the hearing committee was impartial, and that the denial of video evidence without audio did not violate due process. The court affirmed on grounds not reached by the district court. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 20:24:32 Eastern time ET
    Nidian Mendez-Chacon v. Attorney General United States of America (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02323 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02323-0

    FAPD-AI: In Mendez-Chacon v. Attorney General of the United States (3d Cir. No. 25-2323, filed October 27, 2026), the Third Circuit dismissed a petition for review of a Board of Immigration Appeals order denying as untimely a motion to reopen removal proceedings. The court declined to consider an equitable tolling argument that the petitioner had not presented to the Board. It also held that it lacked jurisdiction to review the Board's refusal to reopen sua sponte, because the petitioner did not establish a settled course of adjudication. The disposition is not precedential. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 20:24:32 Eastern time ET
    Michael Hickson v. PECO Energy Co, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01133 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01133-0

    FAPD-AI: In Hickson v. PECO Energy Co. (3d Cir. No. 26-1133, filed October 27, 2026), the Third Circuit granted the private appellees' motion for summary affirmance and affirmed the district court's dismissal of a pro se complaint against a utility company and other defendants. The court held that the federal claims against private defendants failed for lack of state action, that the claims against Commonwealth and City defendants were time-barred under Pennsylvania's two-year limitations period, and that the Internal Revenue Code and the Privacy Act provided no basis for relief. The disposition is not precedential. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 20:24:32 Eastern time ET
    Soto-Fierros v. Blanche (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca5-26-60093 / USCOURTS-ca5-26-60093-0

    FAPD-AI: In a per curiam opinion not designated for publication, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit denied Laura Soto-Fierros's petition for review of a Board of Immigration Appeals order that denied her motion to reconsider the summary dismissal of her appeal as untimely. The court held that the BIA did not abuse its discretion and found no extraordinary circumstance warranting equitable tolling. The opinion stated that counsel's choice to attempt a paper filing instead of using the BIA's electronic-filing requirement, together with a 15-month delay in confirming the appeal's filing, weighed against a finding of diligence. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: In McNellis v. Douglas County School District (10th Cir. No. 26-1020, filed October 27, 2026), the Tenth Circuit reversed the district court's December 22, 2025 grant of summary judgment to the school district on a former Ponderosa High School administrator's religious discrimination claims. The panel concluded that the record, including statements attributed to school officials about the termination and proposed edits to an apology letter, presented a genuine dispute of material fact as to pretext. The case was remanded for further proceedings, and the order is designated not precedential. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-24-09563 / USCOURTS-ca10-24-09563-0

    FAPD-AI: In Cardenas-Gamez v. Blanche, the Tenth Circuit dismissed in part for lack of jurisdiction and denied in part a petition for review of a Board of Immigration Appeals decision affirming the denial of cancellation of removal. The court held that challenges to the agency's factual findings on hardship are unreviewable under Wilkinson v. Garland, and it declined to consider arguments the petitioner did not raise before the BIA. It also rejected the claims that the BIA failed to adequately explain its decision and departed from established precedent. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-24-07073 / USCOURTS-ca10-24-07073-0

    FAPD-AI: In United States v. Williams, the Tenth Circuit affirmed a 96-month sentence imposed on Edward Jay Williams after he pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter in Indian country following a motorcycle accident. The court held that Williams waived his procedural challenge by failing to object in a non-generalized manner. It further held that the district court adequately weighed the 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) factors and explained its upward variance, so the sentence was not a substantive abuse of discretion.     Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ128

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-128, approved October 20, 2026, takes approximately 1,082.63 acres of federal land in Washington State, shown as "NPS Parcels to be Transferred to Tribe" on a December 2021 Olympic National Park map, into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe and includes that land in the Lower Elwha Reservation. The Act exempts the land from valuation requirements, directs the Secretary of the Interior to survey its boundaries, and provides that the land is not Indian lands under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act. It also states that nothing in the Act affects rights under the Treaty of Point no Point of January 26, 1855. PLAW-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-130, approved October 20, 2026, known as the Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025, directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to convey approximately 3.372 acres in Lot 1A, Block 36 East Addition, Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation by warranty deed within two years of enactment. The conveyance requires no consideration, imposes no obligations or conditions on the Foundation, and creates no reversionary interest for the United States, and it supersedes any prior quitclaim deed for the property. The Act provides that the Foundation is not liable for pre-conveyance environmental contamination on the property and requires the Secretary to comply with CERCLA section 120(h). PLAW-SEL-01

    Public Law 119–133: To redesignate the Chiricahua National Monument in the State of Arizona as Chiricahua National Park… (opens in a new tab)
    Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ133

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-133, approved October 20, 2026, known as the Chiricahua National Park Act, redesignates the Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona as Chiricahua National Park, with boundaries unchanged from the monument's boundaries on the date of enactment as shown on a March 2021 map. The Act provides that references in federal law and records to the monument refer to the park and that funds available for the monument are available for the park. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to administer the park under existing presidential proclamations and the laws generally applicable to National Park System units, and to protect traditional cultural and religious sites in consultation with Indian Tribes, including tribal access and temporary closures on request. PLAW-SEL-01

    Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-21932

    official summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2013-01-05, which applies to certain Airbus Helicopters (Eurocopter France) Model AS350B3 and EC130B4 helicopters. AD 2013-01-05 requires revising the Limitations section of the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM) supplement to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amperes (amps) and installing a placard in the instrument panel to indicate the revised limitation. Since the FAA issued AD 2013-01-05, the manufacturer determined the applicability needs to be revised to add helicopters equipped with certain part numbered starter generators and to remove helicopters with certain engines installed. This proposed AD would require revising the Limitations section of the RFM supplement of the existing RFM for the helicopter, to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amps and installing a placard in the instrument panel indicating the revised limitation. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Exemptions To Permit Circumvention of Access Controls on Copyrighted Works (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · LIBRARY OF CONGRESS · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-21939

    official summary: The United States Copyright Office is conducting the tenth triennial rulemaking proceeding under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (“DMCA”), concerning temporary exemptions to the DMCA's prohibition against circumvention of technological measures that control access to copyrighted works. Having carefully considered the petitions for new and renewal exemptions and comments received in response to the June 9, 2026 Notification of Inquiry, the Office announces the Register's intention to recommend all but one of the existing exemptions for renewal, and initiates three rounds of public comment on newly proposed exemptions. Comments submitted may not exceed twenty-five pages per class, excluding documentary evidence. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to establish a temporary special local regulation (SLR) for certain navigable waters of the Miami Shipping Channel offshore of Port Miami, Miami, FL in connection with the E1 Miami Grand Prix. The SLR is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by high-speed powerboat racing. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in or loitering around the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector Miami. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking. FR-SEL-02

    Voluntary Consensus Standards Update; Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-21963

    official summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing a final rule to update the incorporation by reference of several voluntary consensus standards in the Agency's formaldehyde standards for composite wood products regulations under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) due to the standards having been updated or superseded by the issuing organizations. These new standards primarily update test methods and product standards concerning composite wood products that use formaldehyde. EPA is also conforming these updated standards in the scope and definitional sections in the final rule and incorporating by reference a new small scale quality control chamber test method, similar to current methods already incorporated by reference. EPA is also removing one standard that was previously incorporated by reference to avoid redundancy, given that another identical, internationally recognized version of the standard is already incorporated by reference in this rule. FR-SEL-01

    Television Broadcasting Services Elko, Nevada (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-22034

    official summary: This document amends the Table of TV Allotments (table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules by substituting VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 at Elko, Nevada in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by Reno (KENV-TV) Licensee, Inc. (Licensee), the licensee of full power television station KENV-DT (KENV-DT or Station), Elko, Nevada. The Media Bureau (Bureau) previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by the Licensee to substitute UHF channel 20 for VHF channel 10 at Elko in the table, and subsequently granted a construction permit for its new channel. The Licensee states that it was unable to complete construction of the channel 20 facility by the deadline specified in the Station's construction permit. The Licensee filed the instant petition to amend the table to substitute VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 and allow KENV-DT to continue to operate on channel 10 at its licensed parameters and provide uninterrupted service to viewers. The staff engineering analysis finds that the proposal is in compliance with the Commission's principal community coverage and technical requirements, including the interference protection requirements.     Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components Into the United States (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-22049

    FAPD-AI: Proclamation 11074 of October 22, 2026, titled 'Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components Into the United States,' concurs with the Secretary of Commerce's finding under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 that these imports are entering under circumstances that threaten to impair national security. It directs the Secretary of Commerce and the United States Trade Representative to pursue or continue negotiations with foreign trading partners and to report on progress within 180 days, and states that certain wind turbine components made of aluminum, steel, or copper are subject to tariffs under Proclamations 9704, 9705, and 10962. The proclamation cites the Secretary's findings on grid reliability, cybersecurity risks in imported networked inverters, and radar interference. FR-SEL-03

  • Observed at 04:43:22 Eastern time ET
    National Seafood Month, 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-22050

    FAPD-AI: Proclamation 11075 of October 22, 2026, designates October 2026 as National Seafood Month and calls on Americans to express thanks to those who work in the seafood industry and to hold appropriate events and ceremonies. The proclamation summarizes actions taken by the current Administration on seafood, including an Executive Order on seafood competitiveness, the launch of the Department of Agriculture Office of Seafood, three proclamations restoring commercial fishing access in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, and $123.6 million in fishery disaster assistance. It states that the U.S. seafood industry harvests about 8.5 billion pounds of seafood annually, supports more than one million jobs, and generates more than $173 billion in commerce. FR-SEL-03

  • Observed at 04:43:22 Eastern time ET
    Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-22051

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14438 of October 22, 2026, titled 'Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People,' directs the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to establish a pilot program under which Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac proactively cancel mortgage insurance on eligible single-family loans using automated valuation models, and to expand the title acceptance pilot into an ongoing nationwide program for eligible refinances. The order establishes a Task Force on Manufactured Housing Innovation, co-chaired by the Secretaries of Housing and Urban Development and the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which must submit recommendations within 180 days on factory-built housing. It also directs the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to reduce interest rates on single-family loans made directly by their departments, consistent with applicable law and available appropriations. FR-SEL-03

    Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petro… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-10-28 / 2026-22052

    FAPD-AI: Presidential Determination No. 2027-01 of October 22, 2026, addressed to the Secretary of War, determines under section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, that domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity are industrial resources, materials, or critical technology items essential to the national defense. The determination states that industry cannot reasonably provide these capabilities in a timely manner without Presidential action, and it waives the requirements of section 303(a)(1) through (a)(6) for the purpose of expanding such capacity. It authorizes and directs the Secretary to implement the determination, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments, and supersedes inconsistent prior directives to that extent.
